lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: South-West Roads Project: Western Europe-Western China International Transit Corridor (CAREC 1b & 6b), P099270. Loan IBRD-76810 of US$2.125 billion approved 30 April 2009, loan agreement signed 13 June 2009, effective 9 December 2009. Original closing date 31 December 2013, extended four times to 31 December 2024. US$2,102,277,467.99 was disbursed, with a further US$366,300,126 from the borrower, for a total project cost of US$2,468,577,593.99. Environmental category A, triggering the Bank's Involuntary Resettlement policy OP/BP 4.12. Implementing agency the Ministry of Transport. Outcome, Bank performance and the quality of monitoring were rated Satisfactory, Satisfactory and Substantial by the completion report, and the Independent Evaluation Group review gave the same three ratings (World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report, 19 June 2025; Independent Evaluation Group ICR Review, 7 October 2025). On safeguards the two documents do not say the same thing. The completion report states that the project's environmental performance was rated Moderately Satisfactory for much of the implementation period (World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report, 19 June 2025, paragraph 76). The Independent Evaluation Group review broadens that to safeguard compliance, saying it was mostly rated Moderately Satisfactory throughout implementation and was rated Moderately Satisfactory at closing (Independent Evaluation Group ICR Review, 7 October 2025).

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD), safeguards finding
lenders.role: The completion report states that in Kyzylorda Oblast land acquisition began before the Bank cleared and disclosed Resettlement Action Plans and before grievance redress mechanisms were in place, contrary to World Bank policy, and that safeguard readiness at entry was weak (World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report, 19 June 2025). The Inspection Panel's 2011 report records that when the lending instrument was changed at appraisal the project was reclassified environmental category A, which requires the environmental assessment and resettlement plans to be disclosed before appraisal, and that senior Bank management agreed a waiver of that requirement should be sought from the Board of Executive Directors at the same time as approval of the project. The Board approved the waiver on 30 April 2009, the day it approved the loan (Inspection Panel Report and Recommendation, 18 October 2011).

south-west-roads-turkestan-sairam-compen.community: Two requests for inspection were filed over this loan, in 2010 and 2011, and a third in 2020. The 2011 request was brought by Bauyrzhan Isaliev of the non-governmental organisation National Analytical Information Resource on behalf of the organisation and 24 project-affected people, and concerned four places: Turkestan, Sairam, Yntymak and Temirlanovka. In Turkestan, two family members had built a commercial facility in 2008 and intended to open it in 2009. They were told in early 2009 that the road project required them to stop the venture and that they would be compensated. Compensation was not paid. The Panel team was told the dispute turned on paperwork showing the size of the plot and on the absence of technical certificates for the building, which could not be issued without a valid land title. Road works at the site were suspended. The requester told the Panel team he would file a fourth court application to settle his entitlements. In Sairam, eight people holding agricultural land on 49-year state leases said works began on their land before compensation agreements were concluded. Bank Management confirmed that a contractor had moved equipment onto private property and started works on land for which compensation was still disputed and had not been paid, describing the incursion as lasting about one day and involving some initial scraping and removal of topsoil. Management also observed that the requesters did not claim that any material harm resulted from the incursion and proposed no specific remedial measures. By the Panel's visit of 26 September to 1 October 2011, seven of the eight had been paid; the eighth said he had reached an agreement but believed he had accepted less than he was owed. The Panel found the entitlement matrix in the South Kazakhstan Region Resettlement Action Plan appeared to allow one year of lost future income while Kazakh law appeared to require all remaining years of the lease, and that requesters in Sairam said they had never seen the leaflet describing the plan. In Yntymak, a settlement stretching 5 km along the highway out of Shymkent, residents said the designer's stated 35 to 40 metre distance from road to houses was in fact 15 to 20 metres. Bank Management said it could not state whether an appropriate design could be achieved without further land acquisition and population displacement. On Temirlanovka, Management agreed with the requesters that the environmental impact assessment was largely generic and lacked site-specific information and analysis. Over the life of the loan several thousand grievances were handled, covering the quality of workers' accommodation, compensation, restoration of temporarily used land and requests for livestock pens; the Bank team told the Independent Evaluation Group on 29 August 2025 that no exact data on grievances was recorded. The completion report gives no count of households relocated.
south-west-roads-turkestan-sairam-compen.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 7,350 for this project, which is its count of project-affected people and not a count of people moved. No Bank document gives a count of households or people relocated under this loan.
south-west-roads-turkestan-sairam-compen.ecosystem: The project was environmental category A. Bank Management agreed in 2011 that the environmental impact assessment for the Temirlanovka bypass was largely generic and lacked site-specific analysis; requesters said the bypass would damage the Tugai floodplain forest and the Arys river ecosystem. The completion report records contractors with insufficient environmental staffing, inadequate health and safety practices at construction sites and worker accommodation, and delays in rehabilitating borrow pits. The completion report records that ancient burial sites were found along the Otar-Uzynagash section and documented by local archaeologists. The Bank's project team told the Independent Evaluation Group on 29 August 2025 that works were halted, archaeologists were engaged and the finds were transferred to a museum; that account is not in any project document.
south-west-roads-turkestan-sairam-compen.outcome: The 2011 Panel found the request eligible on all six criteria but did not recommend an investigation, noting that Management had shown action was being taken and that the requesters said their concerns were resolved or about to be resolved. A third request was filed on 24 December 2020 by four residents of Shakpak Baba village, Tulkubassiy district, who said eight houses were flooded in 2017 with material damage and only one household was compensated, that wells and a concrete irrigation canal no longer worked, that road accidents had risen and that a cattle crossing under the road was partly blocked with gravel debris. Management said the 2017 flooding followed general snowmelt and rainfall across Kazakhstan rather than the roadworks, and commissioned a hydrological study in January 2021. In its eligibility report of 13 April 2021 the Panel recommended no investigation, finding no plausible link between the project and the 2017 flood, the clogged wells or the lost irrigation water, no material increase in the accident rate at Shakpak Baba, and acceptable maintenance of the cattle crossing culverts, while noting weaknesses in consultation and disclosure. The Board approved that recommendation on 26 April 2021. The loan closed on 31 December 2024 with a 42 km section of the Otar-Uzynagash road still unfinished after the original contract was terminated.

hanoi-ring-road-2-relocation.community: The Ring Road 2 component of the project affected 1,541 project-affected households, of which 714 were relocated. The completion report states that compensating these households was extremely difficult and caused significant delays, that households demanded higher compensation, and that all compensation and resettlement activity was suspended for more than a year while the Hanoi People's Committee waited on an independent land appraisal before approving new land compensation prices, which it did for all four districts with resettlement in September 2013, with a method for setting land prices in 2014. The mid-term review found the project management unit and district authorities had not followed the agreed resettlement framework: households on land treated as illegally occupied received no assistance, the replacement cost paid did not replace what households had lost, the cut-off date was set earlier than the framework required, and unregistered businesses received no assistance. At closing, compensation and resettlement were reported complete except for two outstanding cases, but payment for income losses and help for affected businesses to restart remained very slow, and the Hanoi People's Committee was asked to speed up payment for income losses in Tay Ho, Cau Giay and Dong Da districts and to help affected businesses find new sites. A resettlement site, CT1, was built to house the displaced households. The design of the Dao Tan interchange was changed after residents complained, to reduce the amount of resettlement. The project management unit continued after closing to work with local authorities on supplementary compensation for all relocated households.
hanoi-ring-road-2-relocation.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 7,329 for this project, which is its count of project-affected people and not a count of people moved. The Bank's completion report and the Independent Evaluation Group review both give 1,541 project-affected households including 714 relocated; neither converts either figure into a number of individuals.
hanoi-ring-road-2-relocation.outcome: The credit closed on 31 December 2016 with Ring Road 2 open to traffic. Social safeguards were rated moderately satisfactory at closing by the final supervision mission. Payment for income losses and support for affected businesses to restart were still outstanding at closing and were left to the Hanoi People's Committee and the districts to complete.

bahia-viver-melhor-ii-resettlement.community: Resettlement aimed to move households out of areas of non-mitigable risk into housing no more than 1 km from their original homes. Households were offered cash compensation, assisted purchase of replacement housing described as monitored indemnification, or a move into newly built houses. By closing on 31 October 2013, 1,332 households had been resettled from high-risk or unhealthy areas, against an original target of 983; over the project the number of households in risk areas due for resettlement had risen from 983 to 1,448, which makes the achievement 92 per cent of the revised need. A further 293 households stayed where they were, with risks dealt with by other means. A footnote in the same completion report puts the total number of families resettled at closing, from all causes, at 1,750, of whom 62 per cent took new housing, 21 per cent cash compensation, 12 per cent assisted purchase, and 5 per cent were still in legal proceedings, in the report's words possibly hoping for higher compensation. At closing 832 resettlement cases were still unfinished, reduced to 795 by January 2014. Of those 795, 661 were waiting for a new housing unit, 82 were in judicial compensation proceedings, 26 awaited cash compensation and 26 awaited monitored indemnification. By area the 795 pending cases were 318 at Sao Bartolomeu, 198 at Parque Sao Bartolomeu, 145 at Mangueira III, 123 at Sussuarana III / Baixa da Paz, 10 at Encosta de Piraja and 1 at Avenida Anchieta. Of the 661 awaiting housing, 535 were expected by August 2014 and the rest by August 2015. The housing-conditions indicator reached 1,009 households against a target of 2,000; the project management unit did not count 164 cash compensations in that figure because it could not establish whether the homes those families bought were better than the ones they left or how the money was spent. In the only housing development finished at closing, at Feira de Santana, 14 of 358 families, 4 per cent, sold their new housing; the national figure quoted in the report is 12 per cent.
bahia-viver-melhor-ii-resettlement.displaced_label: families resettled in total at project closing, of whom 1,332 came from high-risk or unhealthy areas
bahia-viver-melhor-ii-resettlement.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 5,768 for this project, which is its count of project-affected people and not a count of people moved. The Bank's completion report carries two counts of people actually resettled: 1,332 households removed from high-risk or unhealthy areas, which is results-framework indicators A2 and A3 measured at 31 October 2013, and a total of 1,750 families resettled at closing from all causes, which is footnote 23 on page 10. The 1,750 is the wider count and is the figure carried here. The Independent Evaluation Group review repeats only the 1,332.
bahia-viver-melhor-ii-resettlement.outcome: The loan closed on 31 October 2013 with all proceeds disbursed and 795 resettlement cases unfinished as of January 2014, most of them households waiting for housing that was promised for August 2014 and August 2015. The Independent Evaluation Group rated the outcome Moderately Unsatisfactory and the risk to the development outcome Significant, and recorded that a non-negligible amount of infrastructure and resettlement work was incomplete at closing. No document found records whether the remaining housing was delivered.

bogota-high-risk-area-resettlement.community: The project paid for moving households out of areas of Bogota classified as non-mitigable risk. The target was up to 700 households earmarked for resettlement to safer places with secure housing tenure; at closing on 31 January 2014, 1,067 families had been resettled, 53 per cent above target. The completion report attributes the overshoot to 367 additional families living in the Nueva Esperanza neighbourhood who were resettled to safer locations with secure housing tenure. The baseline for this indicator was set as 25,000 people living in high risk, and the Bogota District Planning Department assumed for planning purposes that a household contains on average four people. The project required supervision of safeguards because some families were unwilling to resettle, a problem identified by the Bank task team leader and recorded in the Quality Assessment of Lending Portfolio review. The report states that the resettlement was carried out so as to limit disruption to people's livelihoods and that displaced people were treated equitably, citing the 2009 restructuring safeguard note, and that measures were put in place to reduce women's exposure to violence and stress during the move and to avoid breaking up community networks. The report also records that no negative social or environmental impacts were identified at project closing.

bogota-high-risk-area-resettlement.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 4,651 for this project, which is its count of project-affected people and not a count of people moved. The Bank's completion report counts 1,067 households resettled at closing against a target of 700, and notes that the district planning department assumed four people per household for planning.
bogota-high-risk-area-resettlement.outcome: The loan closed on 31 January 2014. The resettlement target was exceeded, and the completion report says the guidelines developed under the loan are now applied to other resettlement processes in Bogota. Two other project targets were not met: no study on insuring public and private assets against disasters was delivered, disseminated or used in planning before closing, and hospital construction reached 57 per cent against a target of 100 per cent.

bogota-high-risk-area-resettlement.confidence_note: The count of 1,067 families resettled and the 367 families at Nueva Esperanza come from the Bank's own completion report, with the Independent Evaluation Group reviewing that report rather than the site.
bogota-high-risk-area-resettlement.dropped_reason: Fails test 2, actual harm. On the completion report's own account the 1,067 families were moved out of areas Bogota had classified as non-mitigable landslide and flood risk, to safer locations with secure housing tenure, as the benefit the loan was bought to deliver: the move was a project target of up to 700 households and the overshoot is reported as success. The report states that livelihood disruption was minimised, that displaced people were treated equitably, and that no negative social or environmental impacts were identified at closing. The involuntary resettlement policy was triggered for land or property acquisition for the construction and retrofitting works, not for this component; the only such acquisition recorded was in the health sector, under an abbreviated plan for fewer than 200 people affected, with no complaint filed. The one sign of compulsion, that some families were unwilling to resettle, carries no count and no recorded loss, so it does not meet limb (b) on its own. No independent account of what happened to the resettled families was found.

baku-shamakhi-highway-land-acquisition.community: The completion report states that the project managed impacts on 441 affected people, including fourteen cases of economic displacement. Compensation came from state funds and was administered by the road administration's specialist department. The project implementation unit was required to ensure that owners and users of the affected land were compensated before works began. The report says the process was lengthy, particularly where landowners could not be traced, and that a few cases were settled only after litigation. A grievance mechanism run by contractors and monitored by supervision consultants recorded complaints; the report names accidental damage to irrigation or drainage pipes, keeping access to land plots, and dust levels as the common ones, most settled on site by contractors. The land acquisition process followed a national expropriation law that had itself been drafted under the earlier World Bank-financed Second Highway Project and adopted by presidential decree in 2010.
baku-shamakhi-highway-land-acquisition.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 3,910 for this project, which is its count of project-affected people and not a count of people moved. The Bank's completion report gives 441 affected people and fourteen cases of economic displacement, and no count of households physically relocated.
baku-shamakhi-highway-land-acquisition.outcome: The project closed on 31 March 2021 after a six-year extension. The completion report records all affected land owners and users as compensated, with a few cases resolved through the courts. No independent account of the land acquisition was found.

baku-shamakhi-highway-land-acquisition.dropped_reason: A card whose content is a count of people affected. Paragraph 110 of the completion report is the whole record: 441 affected people, fourteen cases of economic displacement, a lengthy process where landowners could not be traced, a few cases resolved only after litigation, and a brief 2014 downgrade of the involuntary resettlement rating to Moderately Unsatisfactory that was reversed at the next review. The same paragraph states that before works commenced the project implementation unit ensured that owners and users of the impacted land were fully compensated in accordance with the resettlement action plans, and the Independent Evaluation Group review states that the project complied with the social safeguards. No person, no village, no compensation amount, no litigation outcome, no count of households relocated and no independent source. Limb (b) is not met: nothing in the documents records compensation unpaid, paid below replacement cost, a livelihood not restored or a loss of access to an identifiable person. The coordinate is Shamakhi town, one end of the project road, not a place where land was taken.

lenders.name: World Bank (IDA)
lenders.role: National Roads and Airport Infrastructure Project, P122007. Credit IDA-49230 of US$109.5 million approved 5 May 2011, effective 10 April 2012. The commitment was revised to US$104,005,075 and US$80,588,861 was disbursed; the US$19.7 million of borrower funding originally planned was revised to zero. Original closing date 31 December 2016, actual closing 2 August 2023, after six restructurings. Environmental category B, triggering Indigenous Populations OP 4.10, Physical Cultural Resources OP 4.11 and Involuntary Resettlement OP 4.12. Borrower the Plurinational State of Bolivia; implementing agencies Administradora Boliviana de Carreteras and, from 2022, NAABOL. The project aimed to improve year-round use of the San Buenaventura-Ixiamas national road and the safety, security and operational reliability of Rurrenabaque Airport The completion report rated the outcome and Bank performance Moderately Satisfactory; the Independent Evaluation Group rated both Moderately Unsatisfactory, the outcome because of the weighting applied after restructuring and Bank performance because of shortcomings at quality at entry. Both rated the quality of monitoring Modest (World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report, 31 May 2024; Independent Evaluation Group ICR Review, 4 September 2024).

rurrenabaque-airport-land-compensation.community: Before the World Bank became involved, the local government had expropriated land from two landowners to widen the airport perimeter at Rurrenabaque. The Bank found that payments were still outstanding because the local government and the landowners did not agree on the amount. The Bank hired a third party to value the assets against its safeguard policies. Civil works for the airport component could not start until the land compensation was settled in January 2018, and all works and supervision for that component began only in May 2018. Under the road component the grievance mechanism received 69 cases. All were closed by project closing except three: two concerning a subcontractor's failure to pay suppliers, and one gender-based violence case. The supplier cases were closed after project closing, after the road administration asked the main contractor to require the subcontractor to pay. The gender-based violence case was put into a post-closing action plan; the survivor completed therapy and the legal process against the alleged perpetrator continues. Under the airport component the grievance mechanism received 28 cases; four further complaints about one contractor failing to pay workers and subcontractors arrived after project closing and were followed up by NAABOL and closed. Implementation of the Indigenous Peoples Plans was also delayed, and the last balances of plan funds had to be spent by a technical team assigned by the road administration after the supervision contract ended.
rurrenabaque-airport-land-compensation.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 3,686 for this project, which is its count of project-affected people and not a count of people moved. No Bank document gives a count of households or people relocated; the documented land take is from two landowners at the airport perimeter.
rurrenabaque-airport-land-compensation.ecosystem: The project was environmental category B and triggered Natural Habitats OP 4.04 and Forest Management OP 4.36. The road it financed runs beside Madidi National Park. Clearing 8.5 hectares inside the airport grounds to give the control tower sight of the runway reached an area identified as sensitive, which brought the natural habitat safeguard into play; a flora and fauna survey was carried out and an assisted migration plan was prepared and about 1,500 animals, including amphibians, mammals and reptiles, were rescued under it. In the environmental liabilities restoration programme the number of outstanding liabilities fell from 73 listed in the environmental impact assessment to 18 and then to 13; the rest were closed through agreements between owners and communities. Old bridge beams were left in the right of way of the former Muije bridge.
rurrenabaque-airport-land-compensation.outcome: The credit closed on 2 August 2023 with US$80,588,861 of US$109.5 million disbursed. Social safeguards were rated Satisfactory with shortcomings late in the project, and a post-closing action plan was agreed with the road administration for outstanding commitments, with a five-month schedule. The Independent Evaluation Group records that the pending grievance cases have since been resolved. The gender-based violence survivor completed therapy; the legal case against the alleged perpetrator was still running when the completion report was written.

rurrenabaque-airport-land-compensation.confidence_note: Every fact here is from the Bank's own completion report, with the grievance outcome repeated in the Independent Evaluation Group's review of that report. Both are the lender reporting on its own project, and no independent source on this project was found. The land take is small and precisely described: two landowners, unnamed, with payment withheld over a valuation dispute until January 2018, and the expropriation itself carried out by the local government before the Bank became involved. The documents do not name the contractor or subcontractor in the unpaid-worker and gender-based violence cases, do not say how many workers or suppliers went unpaid, and do not give the compensation amounts for the two landowners. The completion report gives the amount disbursed as US$80,588,861 and the Evaluation Group's data sheet as US$80,588,721.14.

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: National Roads Improvement and Management Program (APL) Phase 2, known as NRIMP-2, P079935. Loan IBRD-75520 of US$232 million approved 13 May 2008, effective 16 April 2009, of which US$187.84 million was disbursed, leaving about 19 per cent undisbursed. Original closing date 31 December 2012, actual closing 31 December 2016, after restructurings on 6 December 2012 and 23 December 2014. Environmental category B, triggering Environmental Assessment OP/BP 4.01, Involuntary Resettlement OP/BP 4.12 and Indigenous Peoples OP/BP 4.10. Borrower the Department of Finance; implementing agency the Department of Public Works and Highways. The Australian Agency for International Development co-financed. Overall outcome was rated Moderately Satisfactory. Safeguards performance fell from Satisfactory at the start to Moderately Unsatisfactory as resettlement problems emerged (World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report, 21 June 2017; Independent Evaluation Group ICR Review, 20 November 2017).

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD), safeguards finding
lenders.role: The completion report records as a clear non-compliance with Bank involuntary resettlement policy that the Department of Public Works and Highways allowed linked road improvement works to proceed without compensation being paid, and states that better safeguards due diligence by the Bank would have identified the problem earlier. The Independent Evaluation Group agreed that better safeguards oversight would have prevented linked works from proceeding without compensation being paid (World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report, 21 June 2017; Independent Evaluation Group ICR Review, 20 November 2017).

companies.name: Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH)

philippines-nrimp2-unpaid-land-claims.community: Late in the project a failure to pay land acquisition claims came to light for linked road improvement works that had been built with Philippine government money next to roads improved under the loan. The completion report attributes this to the Department of Public Works and Highways misunderstanding the Bank's involuntary resettlement policy, which requires compensation claims to be paid before construction starts, even for linked works the loan does not finance. Compensation owed to project-affected persons at two locations was still unpaid when the project closed on 31 December 2016. The agreed remedy included cutting the right of way back to the land actually used, to reduce the amount needed. Resettlement action plan implementation was delayed throughout, and the institutional arrangements between the Unified Project Management Office, the Environmental and Social Safeguard Office and the regional and district offices of the Department, needed to monitor safeguard compliance through multi-partite teams, were set up late; reports arrived late and with critical information missing.
philippines-nrimp2-unpaid-land-claims.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 3,149 for this project, which is its count of project-affected people and not a count of people moved. No Bank document gives a count of households or people relocated, or the number of affected persons at the two locations left unpaid at closing.
philippines-nrimp2-unpaid-land-claims.outcome: By the time the completion report was written in June 2017, the Department of Public Works and Highways had told the Bank that all project-affected persons at one of the two locations had been compensated and that payment for the second was held in escrow pending a court decision. The Independent Evaluation Group records the same position in November 2017, as information the Bank's project team gave the evaluators: the issue was resolved for most affected persons, with a few cases awaiting a court decision and the required funds kept aside in escrow. The same project team told the evaluators that action by the Department had been slowed by changes in field office leadership, including the creation of a new administrative region that took over supervision of the sub-project with the delayed compensation. The loan closed on 31 December 2016 with about 19 per cent undisbursed.

philippines-nrimp2-unpaid-land-claims.confidence_note: The non-compliance finding is explicit in the Bank's own completion report and repeated by the Independent Evaluation Group, which reviews that report rather than visiting the sites; both documents agree on every rating. No independent source was found. What is thin is everything specific: the two locations are not named, the number of affected persons is not given, the amounts are not given, and the outcome of the court case is not recorded. The account of how the delay was prolonged, and the statement that most affected persons have since been paid, come from what the Bank's project team told the evaluators rather than from a project document. The coordinate is one named project road section, chosen because the documents do not say where the unpaid claims arose. Eight contractors were debarred for collusion under the earlier phase of this programme, not under this loan.

colombia-mass-transit-cartagena-vendors.community: The project carried out 28 resettlement action plans across the participating cities. As of December 2012, 23 of those plans were complete and all the properties covered by them had been acquired; five plans were outstanding, one of which, for section 5 of Itagui, was dropped after design changes cut the number of properties needed. US$2.62 million was spent on land acquisition and compensation against a US$3.50 million budget. The completion report names the resettlement of people occupying public space, that is street vendors, as the most significant implementation problem in this area, and says it needs more cooperation between implementing agencies and the participating cities to move vendors out of informal work into formal employment. It identifies Cartagena as the case in point: Transcaribe carried out all the actions required to implement the resettlement plan in line with policy, but the local administration had not executed the plan, which the report attributes to institutional weakness and political instability. The report also states that despite these issues all resettlement processes were satisfactorily carried out in compliance with Bank policy.
colombia-mass-transit-cartagena-vendors.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 1,760 for this project, which is its count of project-affected people and not a count of people moved. No Bank document gives a count of households, people or street vendors relocated; the completion report counts resettlement action plans and properties, not people.
colombia-mass-transit-cartagena-vendors.outcome: The loans closed on 31 December 2012 with the Cartagena system still under construction and not in operation, and with two short tranches of its bus corridor unfinished, one 50 per cent and one 95 per cent complete. The Cartagena street vendor resettlement plan had not been executed by the local administration. A follow-on loan of US$350 million was approved in July 2011 (P117947) to continue funding mass transit in Medellin-Valle de Aburra and Bucaramanga and to support a strategic public transport plan for smaller cities.

colombia-mass-transit-cartagena-vendors.confidence_note: The counts of resettlement plans and the land acquisition spending are from the Bank's own completion report and repeated in the Independent Evaluation Group's review of that report. No independent source on this resettlement was found.
colombia-mass-transit-cartagena-vendors.dropped_reason: The documents do not establish that anyone lost anything. The completion report counts resettlement action plans and properties and never counts people: 28 plans carried out, 23 complete with all their properties acquired as of December 2012, US$2.62 million spent against a US$3.50 million budget. It states that all resettlement processes were satisfactorily undertaken in compliance with Bank policy, and the Independent Evaluation Group repeats that. The Cartagena finding is that Transcaribe carried out all the actions required to implement the street vendor resettlement plan and the local administration did not execute it; neither document says whether any vendor was in fact removed from the corridor, so the recorded fact is an unexecuted plan rather than a harm. Neither limb of the forward rule is met: no count of people or households relocated, and no specific documented harm to identifiable people. No independent source on this resettlement was found.
